title: Intermittent weight checksum mismatch likely due to single-bit corruption - investigation notes
content:
Summary:

This note collects the investigation steps, evidence, and proposed mitigations for an intermittent model weight checksum mismatch observed during a progressive rollout on 2025-11-18. The mismatch manifested only on a small subset of replicas (3/120) and only after the weight files were compressed for storage and decompressed by the prefetcher. The behavior strongly points to transient single-bit corruption (bitflip) during disk write or in-memory transfer rather than a deterministic packaging/compilation bug.

Why this is unusual:
- Only a few replicas returned checksum mismatch errors while peer replicas serving the same manifest were fine.
- Failed shards decode and produce off-by-a-few-token sampling artifacts when used in canary inference runs.
- Checksums in the artifact manifest sometimes matched the on-disk checksum observed on the store node, but the worker process computed a different checksum after decompression.

Detection timeline (high-level):
- 2025-11-18 02:10 UTC: Canary rollout (v1.13.2 -> v1.14.0) started to 5% of pool.
- 2025-11-18 02:18 UTC: SRE alert: model-apply-checksum-failure on region-us-west1 (alert threshold p95 checksums mismatch > 2).
- 02:19–02:35 UTC: On-call manually paused rollout, scaled up fallback replicas, and opened P0 incident SRE-4821.
- 02:40 UTC: Initial triage: observed failures on 3 worker pods (pod-14, pod-68, pod-101); logs show decompression succeeded but per-shard CRC32 mismatch during final verification.
- 03:10 UTC: Repro attempt on pod-14 with same manifest: fetch -> decompress -> checksum yields mismatch reproducibly on that node.
- 03:30 UTC: Replaced worker hardware for pod-14 and retried; new pod applied weights without mismatch.
- 04:05 UTC: Full rollout resumed at reduced rate after temporary mitigation flags.

Logs and evidence (select excerpts):
- Worker log (pod-14):
  - [2025-11-18T02:16:54Z] prefetcher: fetch manifest m-20251118-1143 -> success
  - [2025-11-18T02:17:10Z] store: shard-052 decompress -> success (zstd level 19)
  - [2025-11-18T02:17:11Z] verification: computed_crc32=0x4a2f9b1c expected=0x4a2f9b1d
  - [2025-11-18T02:17:11Z] error: checksum_mismatch shard=052 stage=post-decompress

- On-disk checksum on store node (pod-14 host): 0x4a2f9b1d (matches manifest).
- In-memory checksum in worker process: 0x4a2f9b1c (1-bit difference).

What we ruled out quickly:
- Packaging pipeline: we pulled the tarball from upstream S3 and verified checksums on multiple unrelated nodes; they matched manifest.
- Compression/decompression library bug: we re-ran decompression locally with same zstd version; CRC matched manifest consistently.
- Deterministic weight generation: upstream model artifact verification had been performed during build and upstream checksums were stable.

Hypothesis and likely root cause:
- Single-bit corruption during I/O or memory transfer on affected compute hosts. Evidence: on-disk checksums match manifest but worker process sees a one-bit-lower checksum after decompression. The mismatch resolves when the worker is moved to different host/hardware, and re-apply succeeds.
- Possible contributing factor: a rare SSD controller buffer miswrite or NIC offload issue when transferring decompressed blocks between kernel space and our process buffers. Correlation noted with a noisy kernel firmware update on the host two days prior (host kernel log shows nvme health event: "transient write delay").

Impact summary:
- User-visible: canary inference samples returned garbled tokens in a small fraction of requests for affected replicas during the ~20 minute window. Production rollout paused for ~22 minutes. No customer data exposure.
- Capacity: temporarily had to hold back ~5% of rollout and fallback to previous model variant; no sustained capacity shortage.
- SLOs: minor p99 latency spike due to fallback routing to healthy replicas; no SLO breaches beyond conservative internal limits.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- Paused rollout and aborted additional weight applies to prevent wider exposure.
- Drained affected hosts and re-provisioned worker pods on different hosts.
- Enabled strict-per-shard verification early in prefetch pipeline: compute CRC on store node and verify again after kernel copy.
- Added temporary circuit-breaker to fail weight-apply if per-shard verification fails >1 per host per hour.

Follow-up actions (short-term):
- SRE/Infra to check health records and firmware for affected hosts (assigned to Noah).
- Add a background parity scrub job for recently applied shards during first 24 hours after apply (Greta to prototype).
- Update canary config to bias initial allocation away from hosts with recent NVMe events.
- Create alert for per-host-per-hour checksum_mismatch rate > 0.5 (SRE-4821).

Longer-term mitigations / engineering changes proposed:
1) End-to-end per-shard signed artifact chain: sign individual shards in addition to manifest so workers can verify authenticity and detect silent corruption earlier.
2) Double-checked copy path: compute checksum at three points: store node post-write, prefetcher post-decompress, and after kernel-space->user-space copy. If a discrepancy is found, abort apply.
3) Local memory ECC metrics export: surface host ECC events and NVMe SMART errors into our observability pipeline; create dashboards correlating hardware error events with checksum mismatches.
4) Safe-apply mode: when a host has any recent hardware error, force strict-verify mode for first N rollouts instead of optimistic apply.
5) Work with infra to run soak tests under simulated bitflip conditions (kernel module to flip single bits in test image) to validate runbook and mitigation efficacy.

Runbook additions (draft) - short checklist for oncall when checksum_mismatch alerts fire:
- Acknowledge alert and tag incident SRE-4821 (if not already created).
- Check affected pods/hosts and capture: pod id, host id, kernel version, NVMe SMART, last firmware update.
- Immediately drain pod and re-schedule on different host.
- Fetch stored artifact from S3/registry and verify manifest checksums on two independent machines.
- If on-disk vs in-memory checksums differ, escalate to infra for host hardware diagnostics; mark host as suspect in rollout scheduler.
- Re-run canary on known-good hosts, watch token-level sampling for degradation.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the corruption happening during DMA from kernel to process buffer or earlier during device write? We need an in-situ data-capture tool that computes checksum right after DMA completion in kernel space.
- Why did only specific shard indices (e.g., 052, 127) surface more often? Are there alignment/size boundaries that increase exposure?
- Can we reproduce by stress-testing the NVMe controller under concurrent decompress/write patterns?

Actions assigned (owners and target dates):
- Noah Kim: run host diagnostics and collect historical NVMe events for the cluster (due 2025-11-21).
- Greta Johansson: prototype parity-scrub job and add test harness for simulated bitflips (due 2025-12-05).
- Marco Ruiz: PR to runtime adding triple-check verification points with metrics emission (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842) (due 2025-11-27).
- Aisha Patel: update canary scheduler to avoid hosts with recent NVMe events and author runbook changes (due 2025-11-24).

Notes to self (informal):
- This felt different from earlier manifest-checksum incidents because the store node matched the manifest. Keep in mind: any mitigation that only re-checks store-node checksums won't catch this class of failures.
- Keep canary sizes conservative until parity-scrub and triple-check land.
- Ask infra about enabling ECC logs surfaced via node-exporter; we should treat host ECC events as first-class signals for rollout decisions.

Attachments / links referenced during investigation:
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4821
- Runtime PR for triple-check: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842
- Minimal repro harness (internal gist): gist.redwood/bitflip-repro-20251118 (private)

If you have more logs or were oncall during this incident and saw anything that doesn't match above, drop notes here. We expect to iterate on the runbook and harden the artifact verification path over the next 2–3 sprints.

-- Aisha
